name: Harley-Davidson, Inc.

profile.description: Harley-Davidson is an iconic American motorcycle manufacturer founded in 1903, producing heavyweight cruiser and touring motorcycles. The company operates through three segments: Harley-Davidson Motor Company (HDMC), Harley-Davidson Financial Services (HDFS), and LiveWire (electric motorcycles). HOG also operates the Harley Owners Group (H.O.G.), one of the world's largest brand communities with over 1 million members.

innovation.label: WEAK
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): Harley-Davidson spun out LiveWire as a standalone electric motorcycle brand, but LiveWire generated only $5M revenue in Q1 2026 with a projected $70-80M annual operating loss — an expensive bet with minimal traction [1]. The core HDMC segment saw only -2% revenue decline on -3% wholesale shipments, demonstrating stability but no transformative new products beyond incremental model refreshes [1]. AI Deployment (0/2): No evidence of AI-powered products shipping or quantified AI-driven cost savings. The appointment of a Chief Marketing and Technology Officer signals intent but no specific AI deployment results have been disclosed [2]. Market Share (1/2): Harley-Davidson remains the dominant brand in U.S. heavyweight motorcycles, with Q1 2026 showing 14% North American retail sales growth and 8% global retail growth to 33,500 units [1]. However, retail gains were supported by 22% dealer inventory reduction, and global share is eroding as younger riders gravitate toward Royal Enfield, Indian, and Honda. Product Pipeline (0/2): No specific next-generation products announced with clear timelines. The 2026 outlook guides 130K-135K retail units (mid-single-digit growth) but is framed as a transition year without new platform launches [1]. R&D Intensity (1/1): LiveWire investment and $175-200M guided capital expenditures demonstrate R&D spending above recreational vehicle peers, funding electrification and platform development [1].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Harley-Davidson's purpose — 'More than building machines, we stand for the timeless pursuit of adventure. Freedom for the soul.' — is genuinely distinctive, deeply embedded in American culture, and has guided the brand for over 120 years [3]. The brand IS the identity for millions of riders worldwide; few companies achieve this level of emotional and cultural connection. Community Impact (2/2): The Harley Owners Group (H.O.G.) has over 1 million members globally and represents one of the most successful brand communities in business history. Harley-Davidson rallies, charity rides, the H-D Foundation supporting education and health, and dealership events generate significant community impact [3]. The Supplier Diversity program supports minority-owned and female-owned businesses. Employee Retention (0/2): Significant leadership instability — CEO Artie Starrs, CFO/CCO Jonathan Root, COO Bryan Niketh, and CMO/CTO Matt Ryan are all recent appointments, representing near-total C-suite turnover [2]. No specific employee retention or tenure data available, and recent workforce restructuring raises concerns. Insider Buying (0/2): No evidence of meaningful net insider buying by executives in the last 12 months. The company executed $128M in share buybacks in Q1 2026, but these are corporate repurchases, not personal insider purchases [1].

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on available metrics. Q1 2026 consolidated revenue of $1.17B was down 12% YoY, though the decline was driven by HDFS revenue falling 54% after the retail loan book sale — HDMC revenue was relatively stable at -2% [1]. Net income fell 81% to $25M as operating margins compressed to 2.0% from 12.1% [1]. D/E of 71% is near the 70% target, reflecting the HDFS loan book sale reducing financial leverage [4]. ROE of 7.12% is below the 15% target. Profit margin of 5.34% is positive but thin. Forward P/E of 27.61 reflects analyst expectations of significant earnings decline in FY2026 given HDMC guidance of -$40M to +$10M operating income and LiveWire losses of $70-80M [1][4]. The 3.00% dividend yield with 37.87% payout ratio provides income support. Liquidity check passed: 2.87M avg volume x $24.96 = $71.6M daily.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Harley-Davidson's core business — manufacturing, selling, and servicing physical motorcycles — is structurally immune to AI disruption. The motorcycle riding experience is inherently physical and emotional; AI cannot replace the sensation of riding a Harley or the community bonds formed through H.O.G. events and rallies [3]. Manufacturing involves heavy industrial operations, proprietary engine designs (Milwaukee-Eight, Revolution Max), and a global dealer network of physical relationships that AI cannot displace. The HDFS financial services segment faces some AI exposure in credit underwriting and customer service, but these are enhancement opportunities, not substitution risks. AI Opportunity (0/1): No evidence of meaningful AI revenue generation. The company has appointed a Chief Marketing and Technology Officer to integrate digital capabilities but no AI products or quantified AI-driven revenue have been disclosed [2].

infinite_game.summary: Harley-Davidson possesses one of the most authentic brand purposes in corporate America — freedom and adventure — validated by 120+ years of consistent brand identity and a fiercely loyal rider community. However, the near-total C-suite turnover under CEO Artie Starrs, the 2024 DEI policy reversal under social media pressure, a 'transition year' focused on cost-cutting, and HDMC guidance of near-breakeven operating income suggest a company playing to survive rather than playing to endure. The Just Cause is real but leadership is not currently advancing it.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Harley-Davidson's pursuit of 'freedom for the soul' through motorcycling is a genuine Just Cause that has endured for over 120 years — surviving wars, recessions, near-bankruptcy in the 1980s, and cultural shifts [3]. The brand represents more than transportation; it embodies personal freedom. H.O.G.'s 1M+ members are testament to people joining a cause, not buying a product. However, the aging core demographic (average buyer 50+), declining unit sales, and rotating leadership create doubt about whether the cause still inspires the next generation or shapes strategic decisions.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Harley-Davidson's factory culture and dealer network have historically fostered pride and loyalty, with employees and dealers viewing themselves as part of the Harley family. However, the near-total C-suite reshuffling — CEO Artie Starrs, CFO/CCO Jonathan Root, COO Bryan Niketh, CMO/CTO Matt Ryan, and Chief Brand Officer Marcus Fischer are all recent appointments — creates organizational uncertainty at the leadership level [2]. The workforce restructuring and governance concerns suggest strained trust in the current transition period.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Harley-Davidson's competitive language focuses on brand supremacy and category dominance rather than learning from rivals' strengths. The company has been slow to acknowledge that Royal Enfield, Indian Motorcycle, and Japanese manufacturers offer compelling alternatives attracting younger riders at lower price points. No management commentary references learning from competitors' innovations or using competitive pressure for self-improvement [2].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): The LiveWire electric motorcycle spinout represents genuine existential flexibility — Harley-Davidson recognized that motorcycling's future may be electric and invested in a separate brand identity to pursue it [1]. Q1 2026 LiveWire revenue grew 87% YoY to $5M, showing early traction. However, the $70-80M projected annual loss and minimal market penetration suggest the execution has been poor, and the company has not yet demonstrated willingness to fundamentally reimagine its core ICE business model.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (0/2): The 2024 DEI policy reversal under social media pressure from activist Robby Starbuck — abandoning diversity programs and HRC scoring — demonstrates leadership prioritizing avoiding controversy over standing by principles. The FY2026 HDMC operating income guidance of -$40M to +$10M frames the year as a managed decline rather than a bold investment. No evidence of leadership sacrificing short-term performance for long-term capability building. The $128M Q1 buyback at depressed prices shows financial conviction but not strategic courage [1].

investment_thesis: Harley-Davidson trades at $24.96 ($2.63B market cap) — a modestly recovered price from the $21 level earlier in 2026. Q1 2026 delivered $1.17B revenue with 14% North American retail sales growth and 22% dealer inventory reduction, signaling improving sell-through dynamics [1]. The HDMC segment's -2% revenue decline was relatively stable versus the -54% consolidated HDFS decline driven by the retail loan book sale. The brand's 120+ year heritage, dominant U.S. heavyweight motorcycle position, H.O.G. community of 1M+ members, and 3.0% dividend yield with a conservative 37.87% payout ratio provide a value floor [4]. Management's $150M annual cost savings program and new leadership team under CEO Artie Starrs could restore HDMC profitability, while LiveWire's 87% revenue growth (albeit from a tiny $5M base) shows early electric traction [1].
thesis_continued: The bear case remains substantial. Consolidated revenue declined 12% YoY, net income fell 81% to $25M, and operating margin compressed to 2.0% from 12.1% in Q1 2026 [1]. FY2026 HDMC operating income guidance of -$40M to +$10M signals the motorcycle business may lose money this year, while LiveWire's $70-80M annual loss continues to drain capital without a path to scale. Forward P/E of 27.61 reflects analyst expectations of steep earnings decline, and the PEG ratio of 6.51 implies extremely poor growth-adjusted valuation [4]. The core demographic is aging (average buyer 50+) with no proven formula for attracting younger riders. Near-total C-suite turnover — new CEO, CFO, COO, CMO, and Chief Brand Officer — creates execution risk during a critical transition. The 2024 DEI controversy alienated both progressive and conservative customers, and revenue has contracted from $5.84B in 2023 to $4.32B TTM, suggesting structural decline rather than cyclical softness [1][4].
key_catalysts: $150M annual cost savings program and operational restructuring under new CEO Artie Starrs could restore HDMC profitability from the current -$40M to +$10M guided range
14% North American retail growth in Q1 2026 with 22% dealer inventory reduction signals improving sell-through that could accelerate as new product cycles launch
3.0% dividend yield with 37.87% payout ratio provides income floor, and $128M Q1 share buyback at depressed prices provides EPS accretion at deep value multiples
key_risks: Structural demand decline — aging core demographic (average buyer 50+) and revenue contraction from $5.84B (2023) to $4.32B TTM suggests permanent market share erosion, not a cyclical dip
LiveWire electric motorcycle losses of $70-80M annually drain capital with only $5M quarterly revenue, representing a strategic bet with no clear path to profitability or scale
Near-total C-suite turnover under CEO Artie Starrs creates execution risk during a critical transition year with HDMC operating income guided at breakeven to negative
